title: Startup Research OS domain vocabulary
description: GENERATED FILE. Source of truth: packages/contracts/schema/domain.v1.json. Regenerate with python packages/contracts/tools/generate.py.

AggregationProfileStatus.description: Whether the PARAMETERS of a profile have been calibrated against data. Separate from whether the algorithm is defined: defining equations calibrates nothing. Production scoring requires CALIBRATED.

AttributionElement.description: One required part of a source's attribution obligation. A closed enum because the renderer branches exhaustively: an element it does not recognise must be a contract change, never a silently dropped requirement.

ClaimId.description: An assertion about an Opportunity that evidence can independently support or contradict. Ontology V2.1 §17. STABLE across statement revisions: the text may be rewritten, the identity may not. Distinct from ClaimType, which is an epistemic category and not an identity.

ClaimLifecycle.description: EDITORIAL state, never epistemic. There is deliberately no VALIDATED or REJECTED value: evidence can change, and a lifecycle state derived from EvidenceLevel would freeze a conclusion the evidence no longer supports (Mission 1.2 §38). What a claim is worth is read from its aggregation, never from this column.

ClaimOrigin.description: What PROCESS produced the claim, at the level of kind rather than instance. Deliberately carries no model, provider or prompt name: those change constantly and belong in provenance columns, where a new one does not require a contract change.

ClaimTemporality.description: Whether a claim decays. A property of the CLAIM, never of the source: the same platform can carry an evergreen fact and a trend that is stale in a week. Closed because freshness branches exhaustively over it.

ClaimType.description: How an analytical statement is supported. Never conflated in any output.

ConditionVerification.description: HOW a review condition can be checked. Exists so APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS cannot silently mean 'a collector may run': each condition is satisfied individually, and one that no machine can verify must say so rather than pretending it can.

ConditionVerificationResult.description: The outcome of running a verifier against one review condition. Four values rather than a boolean, because 'we could not establish it' and 'it does not hold' call for different next steps and only one of them is a bug. UNKNOWN never becomes SATISFIED, and only SATISFIED clears the condition.

Confidence.description: How much the system trusts a value or interpretation. Presented as a percentage.

DemandSignalFamily.description: Closed. Signal TYPES within a family are a registry, not an enum.

EvidenceAggregationStatus.description: Whether the numbers in a result may be read as covering the evidence set. A result that silently dropped half its items would be indistinguishable from one that used all of them.

EvidenceDirection.description: How one Evidence record bears on a Claim. Support and contradiction are aggregated SEPARATELY and never averaged together, so this drives exhaustive branching and is closed.

EvidenceId.description: An evidence record with mandatory provenance.

EvidenceIndependenceState.description: What is KNOWN about an evidence record provenance relationship to the rest of the set. UNKNOWN is a distinct third state and is never silently promoted to KNOWN_INDEPENDENT.

EvidenceLevel.description: 0 Hypothesis, 1 Weak, 2 Repeated, 3 Multi-source, 4 Market evidence, 5 Direct validation. Never rescaled, never averaged into a score.

EvidenceObservationCategory.description: WHAT KIND of thing was observed, independent of how strong it is. Gates EvidenceLevel 4 and 5, which quantity of evidence must never reach on its own. Closed because level eligibility branches exhaustively over it.

Independence.description: SUPERSEDED by EvidenceIndependenceState in Mission 1.2. A scalar cannot express WHICH records share an origin, so it could not support the grouping the aggregation framework requires, and it invited q * independence -- discounting instead of grouping, which lets ten discounted duplicates still outweigh one original. Retained so historical references resolve; no column uses it.

LlmTier.description: Logical tier. Business services request a tier, never a provider or model name.

MarketScopeType.description: Geographic scope discriminator. Geographic axis only; segment scoping is A-12 and is NOT modelled.

ObservationKind.description: How one ResearchSession related to a persisted entity it encountered. Promoted to the canonical contract in Mission 1.2: it already governed opportunity observations as a SQL CHECK plus a Python frozenset, which is exactly the drift ADR-009 exists to prevent. Not a scoring judgement.

OpportunityId.description: A domain hypothesis. Not owned by the session that found it. Ontology V2 §12.

PersonalDataRisk.description: How likely the source is to carry personal data. A RISK CLASSIFICATION, not a legal ruling: it records what must be handled carefully and what still needs jurisdiction-specific review. GDPR analysis is separate and remains a human decision.

PolicyAssessment.description: The verdict for ONE activity. Activities are assessed separately because their conditions differ: a source may permit automated API access and forbid commercial use. A single boolean called `allowed` would erase exactly that difference.

PolicyEvidenceType.description: What kind of document supports an assessment. Ordered by the evidence hierarchy: official operator documentation outranks anything else, and nothing below OFFICIAL_* may support an APPROVED state on its own.

Probability.description: Likelihood of an event or outcome.

RegistryRef.description: A reference into an extensible registry. Persists the stable id, never the display name.

RegistryStatus.description: Deprecation, never deletion. A deprecated entry stops being offered for new classification but keeps resolving for historical records.

ResearchContext.description: Value object, not an entity. Serialized as an immutable snapshot on a ResearchSession. Ontology V2 §11.3.

ResearchProjectId.description: Persistent workspace-scoped research objective. Ontology V2 §11.2.

ResearchSessionId.description: The only persisted execution entity. Ontology V2 §11.4. Replaces the retired 'run_id'.

ResearchSessionStatus.description: Session lifecycle. Budget exhaustion is COMPLETED with reduced Research Completeness, never a status. A session that finds nothing is COMPLETED, not FAILED.

ResourceContentOrigin.description: Whether the platform's own licence covers a particular resource. Aggregators republish material they do not own, so platform approval is not resource approval. UNKNOWN exists because it is the common case and must fail closed rather than be guessed either way.

Score.description: An assessed magnitude. NOT interchangeable with Confidence.

ScoreFamily.description: The five families. Never collapsed into a single number, not in an API, a sort key or a badge.

SourceAccessMethod.description: HOW access is technically performed. It says nothing about whether access is PERMITTED: permission is a separate dimension carried by the policy review. BROWSER_AUTOMATION being available never implies it is allowed.

SourceAcquisitionCost.description: The shape of what access costs, not an amount. Concrete prices are versioned configuration because operators change them; a price compiled in here would be wrong within months and would look authoritative.

SourceApprovalState.description: Where a source stands in the governance gate. Closed: collector eligibility branches exhaustively on it, and an unhandled value would mean a source of unknown standing being treated as usable. Public visibility never produces APPROVED on its own.

SourceId.description: A registered external source. Global, not tenant-scoped. Registry contents are D-07, still open.

SourceLifecycle.description: Whether the source itself still exists as a target. Separate from approval: a deprecated source may have been approved, and an active source may never have been reviewed.

UserId.description: A principal. Not a tenant. See ADR-005.

WorkspaceId.description: The tenant boundary. Required on every tenant-scoped contract.
